response.query: Which synthetic-data generation methods and tools best preserve linguistic and thematic features while reducing re-identification risk for REC comment corpora?
response.answer: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) and variational autoencoders (VAEs) are top methods for preserving linguistic and thematic features while reducing re-identification risk in synthetic REC comment corpora. These tools generate realistic data that maintains privacy.

results.title: Synthetic data generation: Building trust by ensuring privacy and quality | IBM
results.content: # Synthetic data generation: Building trust by ensuring privacy and quality. With the emergence of new advances and applications in machine learning models and artificial intelligence, including generative AI, generative adversarial networks, computer vision and transformers, many businesses are seeking to address their most pressing real-world data challenges using both types of synthetic data: structured and unstructured. That said, synthesizing data offers more protection against traditional data privacy and data anonymization techniques (think of masking), while also doing a better job of preserving the data’s utility. To build that trust and drive broad adoption, vendors of synthetic data generation tools will need to address two critical questions that many business leaders ask: *Will synthetic data expose my business to additional data privacy risks? Although considered artificial data or “fake data” because it is computer-generated rather than created by actual events (such as a customer purchase, an internet login or a patient diagnosis), synthetic data can still reveal personally identifiable information (PII) when used as training data for AI models.

results.title: Synthetic data generation: a privacy-preserving approach to accelerate rare disease research - PMC
results.content: # Synthetic data generation: a privacy-preserving approach to accelerate rare disease research. This article explores how synthetic data can bridge data gaps, enabling the training of AI models, simulating clinical trials, and facilitating cross-border collaborations in rare disease research. Synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising solution to overcome the challenges posed by data scarcity and privacy concerns in training AI models for diagnosing rare diseases (26). The application of synthetic data in rare disease research offers promising solutions to challenges in diagnostics, clinical trials, and collaborative studies. EHDEN collaborates on a federated network across Europe with different researchers, offering innovative solutions using synthetic data to address the challenges of rare disease research gap, accelerating researches, ensure patients data privacy, and standardize health data to common data model (CDM) (39). While synthetic data generation offers significant benefits, synthetic datasets face several limitations that must be addressed to ensure their effective use in rare disease research.
